question: Which of the following places served as a prison for Mahatma Gandhi and Sarojini Naidu between 1942-44?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Aga Khan Palace.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Aga Khan Palace was used to imprison Mahatma Gandhi, Sarojini Naidu, and other leaders of the **Quit India Movement (1942-44)**.
 
• **Kasturba Gandhi** and **Mahadev Desai **passed away during their imprisonment at the palace.
 
• The palace became a symbol of the **freedom struggle** and is now a **national monument**.
 
• It is located in **Pune, Maharashtra**, and is an important site of Indian history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Birla House:**

 
 
• It was the iconic residence of Mahatma Gandhi in Delhi, deeply associated with his final moments.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi was tragically assassinated here on **January 30, 1948**, a sorrowful day in India's history.
 
 
 
• **Sabarmati Ashram:**
 
 
• It is located in **Ahmedabad, Gujarat**, this ashram was Gandhi's peaceful home from 1917 to 1930.
 
• It was the starting point of the historic **Dandi March (Salt March)** in 1930, a monumental act of** civil disobedience**.
 
 
 
• **Raigad Fort:**
 
 
• Raigad Fort, majestically perched in Maharashtra, was the proud capital of **Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj.**
 
• Raigad Fort is part of the **Western Ghats**, recognized for its cultural significance and listed as a **UNESCO (World Heritage Site).**
